sourceText: When two objects collide and stick together, the collision is perfectly inelastic. Momentum is conserved: the total momentum before equals the total momentum after. Kinetic energy is not conserved; some of it becomes heat and sound. Example: a 2 kg cart moving at 3 m/s hits a 1 kg cart at rest and they stick. Their common velocity is 6/3 = 2 m/s. The kinetic energy drops from 9 J to 6 J, so 3 J is lost. In an elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved, and the objects bounce apart.
